title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 390
paragraphs: First, at Saïs, he built and completed for Athene a temple gateway which is a great marvel, and in this he far surpassed all who had done the like before him, both in height and size — so large are the stones and of such quality. Secondly, he dedicated great colossal statues and very large man-headed sphinxes, and for restoration he brought in other stones of monstrous size. Some of these he had brought from the quarries opposite Memphis, others of very great size from the city of Elephantine, a voyage of not less than twenty days from Saïs. Of all these things, what I wonder at most is this: a monolithic shrine which he brought from the city of Elephantine. They spent three years bringing it, and two thousand men were assigned to convey it, all of them of the class of boatmen. The length of this shrine outside is twenty-one cubits, the breadth fourteen cubits, and the height eight. These are the outside measurements of the monolith shrine; inside, the length is eighteen cubits and five-sixths of a cubit, the breadth twelve cubits, and the height five cubits. It lies by the entrance of the temple; for they did not draw it inside the temple because, as is said, while the shrine was being drawn along, the master craftsman groaned aloud, seeing that much time had been spent and he was worn out by the labor, and Amasis took this to heart as an omen and did not allow them to haul it any further. Others on the other hand say that a man was killed by it, one of those heaving it with levers, and that it was not drawn in for that reason.
